dedupe_keys.name: bicycles for disaster recovery and relief agent based simulation of micromobility supply distribution in stillwater oklahoma

description: This study by Qianli Qiu, Chen Chen, Katherine Idziorek and Stephen D. Wong, published in Scientific Reports in January 2026 after a 2025 preprint, tests whether bicycles and other micromobility vehicles could distribute relief supplies after a disaster when roads or vehicles are unavailable. Setting and method: an agent-based model of the early recovery phase in Stillwater, Oklahoma, with micromobility as the only delivery mode, varying three operational settings: how many residents take part, how much each vehicle carries and how much each resident receives per delivery. Outcomes: distribution was feasible with a small dedicated group; efficiency peaked with 2% of the population delivering, 18 kg loads and 4 kg of supplies per person per delivery. The authors recommend adding micromobility to disaster relief plans and treating local cycling groups as partners. Format and access: an open-access article. Licence and cost: free, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: a simulated, hypothetical event in one small city; no observed deliveries. The thresholds can set fleet and load parameters for agent-based emergency response and recovery models of last-mile relief. It relates to the bicycles in disaster response synthesis and the Philadelphia transit strike bike share study in the catalogue.
